subject: Throughput anchoring & streaming follow-up — FleetLogic pilot
messages:
From: Tom Harris <tom@fleetlogic.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-10-19T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo: throughput targets & streaming needs

Thanks for the demo this morning. Quick recap from our side and clarifying questions:

- Steady-state: ~3 QPS across our gateway (most requests are 400-800 tokens; average 600 tokens) -> ~1,800 tokens/sec steady.
- Peak: 45 QPS sustained for 2-3 minutes during batch ingests; bursts up to 60 QPS for 30-90s during promotions.
- Streaming: For interactive sessions we stream partial tokens as they arrive; typical session has 1-3 concurrent streams per user, spiking to ~20 concurrent streams at campaign peaks.
- Latency SLO: 95th percentile target for user-facing interactions is 250ms if possible; we can accept up to 400ms for complex responses. Background scoring can be 2-3s.

Attached: fleetlogic_sample_payloads.csv and peak profile PDF. Can you confirm whether Redwood's batching and prefix cache can meet the stated peaks without excessive cost? Also need a rough GPU footprint estimate for an initial pilot and for production at our projected traffic.

Thanks,
Tom Harris
Head of Product
FleetLogic

PS: I uploaded sample request logs to the Drive link in case that helps.

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Tom Harris <tom@fleetlogic.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-10-19T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: throughput targets & streaming needs

Tom — thanks for the crisp recap and the attachments. High level answers, and proposed next steps below.

Summary answers:
- Batching + prefix/KV cache: yes, both help reduce unit compute for requests sharing prefixes. For your mix (avg 600 tokens, moderate prefix reuse) we expect 20-35% token-cost reduction with prefix cache enabled and request-aware batching.
- Streaming: Redwood supports streaming tokens and maintains KV cache across streamed requests; streaming increases latency sensitivity but can be handled without sacrificing throughput if concurrency and batch windows are tuned.
- Latency: hitting 95p ~250ms will depend on model choice and GPU type. For a small-scale pilot we can aim for 95p < 400ms with an optimized 7B-13B variant; hitting 250ms likely requires faster GPUs or smaller models.
- Pilot footprint: rough pilot estimate below after we see sample payloads and concurrency breakdown.

Action items / next steps:
1) Please share a 24h sample of request logs and a small sample of real payloads (looks like you attached them, thank you).
2) Clarify concurrency distribution: how many concurrent requests/streams at steady-state vs peak (per region).
3) Agree a short pilot SLO matrix: target 95p latency, target QPS, and cost envelope.
4) Schedule a sizing call: propose 60-minute deep-dive. Calendar: https://cal.redwood/sizing-60

We can produce a quick pilot sizing doc (GPU count range, recommended model family, batching strategy) within 48 hours once we have the logs and the clarified concurrency numbers. Marissa and Rishi — looping you in to own the pilot sizing and cost estimate.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

----
Evelyn's internal note: I will run a quick cost/back-of-envelope before the sizing call and share a one-pager for FleetLogic.

From: Tom Harris <tom@fleetlogic.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Cc: FleetLogic SRE team <sre@fleetlogic.com>
Date: 2027-10-19T12:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: throughput targets & streaming needs

Evelyn — thanks, that plan works. A couple clarifications from the SRE team attached:

- Concurrency: steady-state concurrency across users is low (avg ~6 concurrent requests across the fleet), but during campaigns we see 350-450 concurrent active sessions (resulting in the 45 QPS sustained).
- Streams per session: normal interactive session opens 1-3 streams; campaigns push that up to 15-25 streams briefly.
- Payload characteristics: median request 520 tokens, 75th percentile 720 tokens. We put a short CSV in Drive with percentiles.
- Regional split: 85% us-east, 10% eu-west, 5% ap-southeast.

Drive link: https://drive.company/fleetlogic/payloads (same as earlier). The team says pilot budget can support 2-3 dedicated GPUs for a 2-week pilot if that helps with concrete numbers.

Tom Harris
Head of Product, FleetLogic

--- Forwarded attachment list ---
- fleetlogic_sample_payloads.csv (3.2KB)
- fleetlogic_peak_profile.pdf (1.1MB)

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-10-19T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Post-demo: throughput targets & streaming needs — internal plan

Folks — forwarding FleetLogic's details. Quick internal plan and recommended ask for the sizing call:

1) Data we need before the call (confirm 24h logs uploaded):
   - 1 minute QPS distribution (histogram)
   - request token percentiles (they provided CSV)
   - concurrent streams time-series for campaign windows

2) Pilot recommendation (to propose to FleetLogic):
   - Pilot model: optimized 13B quantized variant (good balance of latency and quality for their token sizes).
   - Pilot infra: 2x A10s (or 1x A100 40GB equivalent) with dedicated pool, autoscale disabled for controlled testing; cost estimate for 2-week pilot included in our one-pager.
   - Batching strategy: small sliding batches for steady-state (targeting 50-80ms batch window) and dynamic batch widening during short peaks.
   - Prefix caching: enable for repeated prompts; estimate 25-30% compute reduction given their percentiles.

3) Production sketch (ballpark to discuss):
   - For sustained production at their projected peaks with regional distribution, ballpark 4-6 A100-40GB equivalents across us-east with regional failover; implement model fallbacks for cost-sensitive routes.

4) Risks / open questions to settle on sizing call:
   - Whether streaming concurrency will require separate pool vs request generation (affects GPU memory because of KV cache).
   - Their acceptability of slightly higher 95p latency in return for lower cost.

Next steps: Marissa — can you draft the 48h pilot one-pager (technical + cost) and include a short runbook for the sizing call? Rishi — can you prepare an initial GPU-count estimate and list of tests we want to run during the pilot (latency walk, burst soak, cache-effect validation)? I will coordinate the sizing call with FleetLogic and send proposed times.

Thanks — EV

Evelyn Hart
Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
